items.title: COP31 ends without deal after climate change talks break down - ABC News
items.excerpt: ## In short: This year's UN climate summit has ended without a deal after debate broke down over a draft which failed to mention fossil fuels. The deal, put forward by COP31 presidents Australia and Türkiye, was rejected by a host of nations after debate went two days overtime. The summit's failure to reach a new deal does not erase UN climate obligations agreed to in previous conferences. ... The main deal was rejected on Sunday afternoon, local time, by a host of nations, 44 hours after the summit's official close and following two weeks of negotiations. It marked the longest UN climate summit ever. In a chaotic finale to the talks in the Turkish city of Antalaya, debate continued in overtime until COP31 presidents Australia and Türkiye confirmed they would not put forward another draft of the deal. Several countries and the 27-nation European Union said they could not accept the final proposal from the joint Turkish-Australian leadership that did not mention fossil fuels, slamming it as too weak. "We will not endorse a cover decision … that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's climate minister, Darragh O'Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. Developing countries also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet. The deal had called for a tripling of such finance, but did not specify from what baseline. A significant number of nations supported the proposal, even reluctantly, saying that consensus was more important. Any pact approved at the talks requires a near-unanimous consensus. Russia and Saudi Arabia, however, supported the decision to leave the explicit mention of fossil fuels out of the final deal. ... While a blow to efforts to ratchet up international action, the failure to agree a political declaration in Antalya does not erase the obligations agreed by previous UN conferences or remove the technical and legal frameworks governing multilateral action against climate change.

items.title: Economic Week Ahead: Inflation, GDP and Jobs Data Follow Wall Street Selloff | Investing.com
items.excerpt: ## (1) PCED October’s core PCED (Wed) follows September’s 0.3% m/m gain. The Cleveland Fed’s Inflation Nowcasting tracking model projects another 0.3% m/m for both core and headline PCED. That would lift the y/y rates to 3.2% and 3.8% from September’s 3.1% and 3.6%. The core PPI final demand for personal consumption rose 4.8% y/y in October, well above the core CPI’s 2.6% (chart). PCED computers and peripheral equipment rose 9.7% y/y in September, up from August’s 8.4%. PPI electronic components rose faster, to 31.8% in October from September’s 26.8%, widening the gap (chart). That points to a continuation of elevated inflation in tech goods in the coming months. ## (2) GDP The second estimate of Q3 GDP (Wed) follows the advance estimate of 3.4% saar, with the GDP price index up 2.3%. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimates Q4 growth at 3.2% as of November 18, led by a 12.2% jump in business equipment spending (chart). A modest cyclical slowdown is possible through mid-2027. Growth has rested on a robust consumer, strong business spending, and a federal deficit near 6% of GDP during an expansion. Both consumer spending and business investment are likely to slow, with data center activity at risk after the midterms. Earnings growth should slow in tandem. The slowdown should be modest. It means the Fed won’t need to move far into restrictive territory, but it still needs to get back to neutral with a 50bps increase in the federal funds rate, in our opinion.

items.title: Weekly Market Recap | J.P. Morgan Asset Management
items.excerpt: 23/11/2026 ... Thought of the week U.S. inflation remains elevated, with price pressures extending beyond energy into a wider range of goods and services. Core CPI rose 0.3% for the third consecutive month in Oct, highlighting the persistence of underlying inflation. Shelter remained the largest contributor, while transportation, recreation and medical care services also added to price pressures. Meanwhile, higher energy and import costs, alongside the delayed effects of earlier tariffs, are gradually filtering through to consumer prices as businesses seek to recover rising operating expenses. Although moderating wage growth may provide some relief, the lagged impact of earlier cost increases could keep inflation elevated even as the initial energy shock fades. Looking ahead, broadening price pressures across goods and services may complicate the Federal Reserve’s path towards its 2% inflation target.

items.title: Jay Clayton to act as national cyber director until Kirsten Davies confirmed
items.excerpt: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned. - A White House official said the strong support Davies received convinced Trump to nominate her to lead the office permanently rather than keep her in an acting capacity. Why it matters: Clayton, the nation's top intelligence official, will now coordinate cybersecurity policy as outages and reported cyberattacks expose vulnerabilities in America's digital infrastructure. Catch up quick: President Trump announced Thursday he was tapping Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to replace Sean Cairncross as national cyber director. - Davies will assist Clayton as a senior adviser in the Office of the National Cyber Director until she is confirmed. ... The big picture: Two critical national security roles will temporarily fall under one official as President Trump shakes up his cybersecurity team amid the growing threat of AI-powered attacks. - The disruptions have raised concerns about the vulnerability of the nation's digital infrastructure, although administration officials say there is no evidence they were caused by coordinated cyberattacks. - Clayton himself has played a prominent role in the administration's response, telling lawmakers Wednesday that the outages appeared to stem from unrelated technical problems and system upgrades.

The project was later shelved in 2023 (see "'Grendel' Dead at Netflix"). Bobak Esfarjani, who work on Alien: Earth, has been tapped to write, executive produce and act as showrunner for the series. Disney+ announced casting for their new Afterlife with Archie series, according to Deadline. Vasco Faria has been cast as Archie Andrews, Aliyah Mastin plays Veronica Lodge, Sarah Abbott plays Betty Cooper, Angel Rivera is Jughead Jones, and Sabrina Spellman will be played by Chloe Avakian. This series is based on the popular horror comic book series of the same name, in which zombies infest Riverdale (see "'Afterlife With Archie'"). Sony Pictures will release Spider-Man: [Brand-New] Brand New Day into theaters on December 4, 2026, according to The Hollywood Reporter. This rerelease of the blockbuster summer release (see "'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Claims #2 All-Time") includes 10 minutes of new footage. The new footage features a scene in which Rosario Dawson appears as the Night Nurse. Prime Video released a final trailer for Blade Runner 2099 (see below). This limited series, starring Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh (see " 'Blade Runner 2099'"), will hit streaming on November 25, 2026.

items.excerpt: Miley Cyrus marries rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate Palm Springs wedding Singer Miley Cyrus has married rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate ceremony in Palm Springs, California. Cyrus shared news of Saturday's wedding on Instagram, showing photos of the couple embracing in front of a white backdrop with a palm tree. Cyrus wore a long-sleeve silk Saint Laurent gown, while Morando sported a single-breasted tuxedo and dark sunglasses. The pair have been together since 2021, when they met on a blind date. Morando plays for the band Liily. A resurgent ‘Hunger Games’ goes big at the box office, despite competition of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' NEW YORK (AP) — “The Hunger Games” movie franchise rediscovered its box-office might, as “Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted with an estimated $120 million in North American theaters over the weekend. The sun had seemed to be setting on “The Hunger Games” as a cultural force. The previous chapter, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” grossed about half as much as the Jennifer Lawrence-led films. But “Sunrise on the Reaping” launched with $225 million globally, and it did it while a significant portion of potential moviegoers were locked at home playing “Grand Theft Auto VI.” Amazon MGM Studios’ “I Play Rocky” came in second with $9.3 million. Peter Farrelly's comic drama about the making of “Rocky” scored a rare “A+” CinemaScore.
